review.headline: A Petrov where the opponent hung a piece and then walked into a forced loss

sections.text: You won a pawn early with 3...Nxe4 and followed with 4...d5. After 5.Bb3 Be7?! 6.Re1 O-O 7.Nxe5 you were fine.
7...Re8?? (-3.6) was a mistake that left a piece to be won. 7...Nc6 was the engine's choice. But 8.Nf3?? gave it all back (+0.5), since 8.Rxe4 was needed.
You played 8...Bc5?! 9.d4 Bf8 10.c4 c6, then 12...Nxc3 13.bxc3 bxc5 took a pawn. White tried 14.Ne5 c4 15.Ba4 and your 15...Bb7? (-0.9) was a bit loose.
16.Qf3?? was the real blunder, and 16...f6! was a strong answer. 17.Ng4?? then allowed a forced win for you. White resigned soon after.

review.turning_point: 16.Qf3?? and your 16...f6! answer, then 17.Ng4??, moved the game from -0.9 to a forced win.
review.focus: 7...Re8?? left a piece to be won. When the opponent captures on e5 with 7.Nxe5, protect your e4 knight first; 7...Nc6 was the safe move.

review.headline: A Philidor where 10.Bxe4?? gave you a big edge, but 15...Qf6 and a resignation ended it

sections.text: You played the Philidor Nimzowitsch with 3...Nf6 4.dxe5 Nxe4 5.exd6 Bxd6, and the position was equal. 6...Qe7?! and 7...f5? were inaccurate, because the simple 7...Nf6 8.Re1 Be6 kept things safe.
After 8.Nc3 O-O 9.Nxe4 fxe4, White blundered with 10.Bxe4??, and you found the best reply, 10...Qxe4!, which took the bishop. The evaluation jumped to +4.5.
You kept going with 11.Re1 Qg6 12.Qd5+ Kh8 13.Nd4 Bh3 14.g3 Nd7, and White's pieces were all over the board. At 15.Ne6 you were at +6.5.
15...Qf6? was a mistake, since 15...Rae8 was stronger, but you were still at +3.6 when the game ended in a resignation. That was an early end to a position that was still good.

review.turning_point: 10.Bxe4?? gave you a winning position, and 10...Qxe4! took it. The only slip was 15...Qf6?, and you were still ahead when the game ended.
review.focus: At 15...Qf6 the move 15...Rae8 16.Be3 Bxe6 kept your advantage. In a good position, keep playing instead of resigning, because the evaluation was +3.6 for you.

review.headline: A Colle that went wrong in the middle, then a sharp queen finish

sections.text: You played the Colle with 1.d4, 2.e3 and 3.Nf3, and 4...Bxf3 5.Bxf3 gave you the bishop pair. 6.c4 and 7.Nc3 built a good centre, and 8.cxd5 exd5 left you with an edge.
9.O-O?! was a little slow, and 9...Be7? missed 9...cxd4. But 10.Re1? let it slip, since 10.dxc5 was better. 11.Qb3? c4 chased your queen away, and the position was about equal.

12.Qxb7 took a pawn, and 12...Na5?? was a blunder. Your 13.Qb5! was the best answer, hitting the a5 knight, and 14.Qa4 Nc6? let you play 15.Qxc6!, taking the knight. 16.Nxd5 then took another pawn and 16...Ra6 ended the game.

review.turning_point: 14...Nc6? left the knight loose, and 15.Qxc6! took it, taking the evaluation from +2.0 to +4.3.
review.focus: 10.Re1? and 11.Qb3? let a good position go equal. At 10.Re1 the engine wanted 10.dxc5, so exchange in the centre before spending time on other moves.
